Soil Health Card Scheme

Agriculture Support

The Soil Health Card scheme provides farmers with a printed report card showing the nutrient status of their soil and recommendations on the right dosage of fertilizers for better crop yield.

Last updated: 2026-09-18

Main Benefit

Farmers receive a Soil Health Card every 2 years showing the status of 12 key soil parameters — nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, electrical conductivity, organic carbon, and micronutrients like zinc, iron, copper, manganese, and boron. Based on these results, the card provides crop-wise nutrient recommendations so farmers can apply the right type and quantity of fertilizers, reduce input costs, and improve soil health and crop yield over time.

Eligibility

  • All farmers across India — individual cultivators, tenant farmers, and sharecroppers
  • Farmers with cultivable land in any state or UT where the scheme is implemented
  • No income, age, or landholding size restrictions
  • Both loanee and non-loanee farmers are eligible

Required Documents

  • Aadhaar card
  • Proof of land ownership or cultivation (land records, pattadar passbook, or lease agreement)
  • Mobile number for registration and updates
  • Bank account details (in some states, linked to subsidy schemes)

How to Apply

Farmers can apply for a Soil Health Card through their nearest Common Service Centre (CSC), Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), state agriculture department office, or designated soil testing laboratory. In many states, village-level camps are organized where soil samples are collected directly from farms. The process involves soil sample collection, laboratory testing, and card generation — typically taking a few weeks. Some states also allow online registration through their agriculture department portals.

How to Check Status

Farmers can check their Soil Health Card status and download their report through their state agriculture department portal or the national Soil Health Card portal (soilhealth.dac.gov.in) using their Aadhaar number, registration number, or land details. The card shows test results, nutrient status ratings, and crop-specific fertilizer recommendations.

Official Government Source

Soil Health Card Official Portal (soilhealth.dac.gov.in)

Verify with Official Source

Important: Scheme rules, benefits, and deadlines can change. Always verify current information with the official government source linked above before applying.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Soil Health Card?

A Soil Health Card is a printed report card that shows the nutrient status of a farmer's soil and provides crop-wise recommendations on fertilizer dosage. It helps farmers understand what their soil needs for better crop production.

What parameters are tested in a Soil Health Card?

The card tests 12 key parameters: nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH level, electrical conductivity (EC), organic carbon, and micronutrients including zinc, iron, copper, manganese, and boron.

How often is a Soil Health Card issued?

Soil Health Cards are typically issued every 2 years so farmers can track changes in soil health over time and adjust their fertilizer use accordingly.

Who is eligible for a Soil Health Card?

All farmers across India are eligible — individual cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, and farmers of any landholding size. There are no income or age restrictions.

How do I get a Soil Health Card?

Farmers can apply through their nearest Common Service Centre (CSC), Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), state agriculture department office, or designated soil testing laboratory. Many states also organize village-level camps for soil sample collection.

Is the Soil Health Card free?

Yes, the Soil Health Card scheme is a government initiative and the card is provided free of cost to eligible farmers. Soil sample collection and testing are done at no charge.

How does the Soil Health Card help reduce fertilizer costs?

By showing the exact nutrient status of the soil, the card helps farmers apply only the fertilizers their soil actually needs, in the right quantities. This prevents over-application of fertilizers, reduces input costs, and avoids soil degradation from excess chemical use.

Can I download my Soil Health Card online?

Yes, in most states farmers can download their Soil Health Card from the state agriculture department portal or the national Soil Health Card portal (soilhealth.dac.gov.in) using their Aadhaar number or registration details.

What should I do if my soil shows low organic carbon?

Low organic carbon indicates poor soil health. The Soil Health Card typically recommends adding organic matter through compost, farmyard manure, green manure crops, or crop residue incorporation. Following these recommendations over time can improve soil organic carbon levels.

Does the Soil Health Card cover all types of soil?

Yes, the scheme covers all soil types across India. The testing parameters and recommendations are standardized but the specific advice on the card is tailored to the actual test results of each farmer's soil sample.
